children: has intersected broad zones of shallow high-grade gold mineralisation across multiple lodes in diamond drilling at the Goldenclad prospect within its Spur project in New South Wales.

Drilling tested beneath numerous historic gold workings to investigate the continuity of mineralisation across a high-priority six-kilometre target zone at the margin of the Cargo Intrusive Complex (CIC).

Partial results from hole GCD002 along a previously undrilled zone of outcropping mineralisation known as the Wollard’s Line returned best assays of 10 metres at 12.18 grams per tonne gold from 49m within 17m at 7.35g/t and 20.7m at 0.55g/t gold from 11.3m including 2m at 1.76g/t from 30 m.

Hole GCD003 at the Goldenclad Line delivered 7m at 2.58g/t gold from 51m within 13m at 1.51g/t from 48m, 7m at 5.66g/t gold from 85m within 28m at 1.57g/t from 84m, and 7m at 2.68g/t gold from 137m within 32.3m at 1g/t from 123m.

The district appears to contain multiple mineralised structures associated with the margins of the CIC, with recent exploration supporting the concept of a wider corridor linking Ironclad, Goldenclad, Spur, and Consols.
Executive chair Andrew Stewart said the latest results delivered high-grade gold close to surface while providing further evidence of the scale and potential of the broader Goldenclad system.
“While drilling at Goldenclad remains at an early stage, our geological team is systematically defining the controls, continuity and architecture of the mineralised system,” he said.

“GCD002 is particularly significant as the first drill test of the Wollard’s Line and has given us an exciting new high-grade result from a separate mineralised trend that remains open for further testing.”
“GCD003 was designed to test for multiple lodes within the Goldenclad Line and has intersected three significant gold zones within the top 155m.”

“These early results indicate a similar emerging theme to that observed at the Consols and Spur gold zones, being multiple gold-bearing lodes within a broader mineralised system, and provide significant scope to expand the mineralised footprint beyond the current mineral resource estimate.”
Waratah has received firm commitments to raise $50 million to support an ongoing exploration program aimed at growing the Spur project’s 3.1-million-ounce gold resource.
Strong demand from new and existing institutional, sophisticated, and professional investors will see the company issue 76.9 million new and fully paid ordinary shares priced at $0.65 each.
The funds will underpin more than 100,000m of drilling over the next 12 months using 12 diamond rigs to aggressively pursue resource growth.
“Our immediate focus is to convert this funding into metres drilled and then into additional ounces and ultimately build a substantially larger resource at Spur,” Mr Stewart said.
“At the same time, we will continue metallurgical and geotechnical work and broader exploration across at Ironclad, Goldenclad, Alpine, and Gazzards.”

“The strong support from existing shareholders and a select group of new and long-only global specialist resources investors is a significant endorsement of our strategy and the scale of the opportunity at Spur.”

title: Waratah Minerals Delivers High-Grade Gold Assays from Drilling at Goldenclad Prospect
